tagline: From the coke ovens over gravel to orchard country.
intro: Out of Carbondale, below the twin summits of Mount Sopris, CO 133 goes up the Crystal River to Redstone and over McClure Pass at 8,755 feet into the valley of the North Fork of the Gunnison. From there the loop takes in Crested Butte and Gunnison, Crawford and Paonia, 205 miles with the Black Canyon of the Gunnison at the far end.

Coal built Redstone. At Redstone John Osgood put up 84 cottages for his miners and cokers, all with indoor plumbing and electricity, and a 42-room Tudor mansion for his second wife. Down the North Fork, around Paonia, the orchards grow peaches, apples and cherries.

moments.title: Redstone Coke Ovens
moments.text: Ninety of the original two hundred beehive ovens stand in a 600-foot arc beside the highway, idle within ten years of their building and later lived in by hippies.

moments.title: Kebler Pass
moments.text: Between Route 133 and Crested Butte the pavement mostly quits, and County Road 12 crosses the pass at 10,007 feet on gravel.

moments.title: Paonia
moments.text: Samuel Wade brought peony roots here in 1881 and wanted the town called Paeonia, but the post office would not allow the extra vowel.

practical: The 31-mile gravel section over Kebler Pass is closed in winter.
